land.text: Đàng Trong, the Lê court's south (Thuận Hóa, Quảng Nam and the coast to Phú Yên), without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

predecessors.note: The page's lords list begins with Nguyễn Hoàng in 1558 and its infobox has the Nguyễn as 'Subordinates of Trịnh lords (1558-1627)' and a 'de jure fief within the Lê dynasty (1558-1777)'. Cliopatria's Lê row ends in 1571 and this row begins in 1572, so the map separates them in 1572.

land.text: Gia Định and the Mekong delta, the last Nguyễn land, taken by the Tây Sơn in 1776-1777 (without Panduranga and the uplands)

successors.note: Tây Sơn page: 'in 1776 the Tây Sơn army captured the last Nguyễn stronghold of Gia Định'; Nguyễn page: 'By 1777, Gia Định was captured and nearly the entire Nguyễn family was killed'. [fx-42: the Tây Sơn hold the delta again from 1782 and for good from 1785, after the lords' rump of 1778-1782 (ledger/34-39); the lords now end in 1785.]

land.text: Gia Định, regained by Nguyễn Ánh

successors.note: The infobox runs the lords 1558-1777 and 1780-1802 and names the Nguyễn dynasty as successor. Nguyễn Ánh, the one who 'managed to flee to Siam', attacked the Tây Sơn from Siam in 1780 and 'came back to Đại Việt' in 1788, reclaiming most southern provinces (footnote); this dossier stops at 1777 and the restored line is the nguyen-dynasty dossier's. [fx-42: the lords' rump (Nguyễn Ánh, Nguyễn vương) now runs to 1785; the dynasty dossier starts on 7 September 1788 with the same land.]

capitals.name: Trà Bát (Quảng Trị)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Ái Tử (1558-1570)', 'Trà Bát (1570-1600)'; Ái Tử is before this dossier's 1572 start. Coordinates are the district, to a few kilometres.

capitals.name: Phước Yên (Thừa Thiên)
capitals.note: The page text says Nguyễn Hoàng moved to Phú Xuân in 1636 while the infobox has Phước Yên 1626-1636 and Phú Xuân from 1687.

capitals.name: Phú Xuân (Huế)
capitals.note: Taken by the Trịnh in February 1775 (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page).

capitals.name: Quảng Nam (Hội An)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Quảng Nam (1775)'; the Nguyễn 'retreated to Quảng Nam, and later to Gia Định' (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page). Coordinates are Hội An, my reading of 'Quảng Nam'.

capitals.name: Gia Định (Saigon)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Gia Định (1775-1777, 1780-1783, 1788-1802)'; capital in exile at Bangkok 1785-1788. [fx-42: to 1783, the infobox's 'Gia Định (1775-1777, 1780-1783, 1788-1802)'; 1778-1779 are not in the infobox but Ánh held Gia Định from 1778 (Quang Trung page).]

rulers.name: Nguyễn Hoàng
rulers.title: lord (chúa)
rulers.note: Page table: 1558-1613 (the text: he ruled the south for 55 years). The reign begins in 1558, before this dossier's 1572 start, so the strip here starts at 1572.

rulers.name: Nguyễn Phúc Ánh
rulers.title: heir, Nguyễn vương from 1780
rulers.note: The one nephew who 'managed to flee' in 1777 (Nguyễn lords page); 'proclaimed himself Nguyễn vương' in 1780 (Gia Long page); a refugee in Siam from 1785. [fx-42]

keyframe_review.note: 1572-1652: Cliopatria's 296 cells (89,944 km2) are 163 coastal cells (Quảng Bình to Phú Yên plus four of Khánh Hòa) and 133 Central Highlands cells (Kon Tum 36, Gia Lai 55, Đắk Lắk 42), about 45% of the area, which run unchanged through every later keyframe to 1773. No page opened (Nguyễn lords, Cochinchina, Tây Sơn dynasty, Nguyễn Nhạc, Trịnh–Nguyễn War, Panduranga) puts Kon Tum, Gia Lai or Đắk Lắk under the Nguyễn, and the Nguyễn lords and Cochinchina pages are silent on the highlands, so those cells are dropped as unattested (they draw as nobody's land). The page gives no area, so the infobox check could not be made. Two points left as drawn: (1) the Panduranga page has Champa 'attempt to retake land from the Nguyen lord' in Phú Yên in 1611, so the Nguyễn held Phú Yên before 1611 (the sibling champa dossier dates the loss of Phú Yên to 1611); (2) the page both says the 1611 army 'annexed the entire Kauthara Principality' and that Kauthara 'was lost to the Nguyen after a counterattack in 1653', so Khánh Hòa is uncertain 1611-1652 and the four northern cells are kept. The northern edge (18.16 N) is Hoành Sơn, nine cells north of the Gianh River the Trịnh-Nguyễn War page gives as the peacetime line.

correction.text: Quảng Bình to Phú Yên and four cells of Khánh Hòa, without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells
shape unchanged apart from the highlands; applies 1653-1655 (Hà Tĩnh held from 1653); from 1656 the 1659 outline (new keyframe nguyen-lords_1656)

keyframe_review.note: Years only: applies 1653-1655. 100,615 km2 with Hà Tĩnh (18 of 19 cells) and Khánh Hòa to 11.8 N: 'The Nguyễn invaded the north and captured Quảng Bình, then Hà Tĩnh' in 1653 and 'the Kauthara principality was lost to the Nguyen after a counterattack in 1653' (Panduranga page). The Nguyễn were 'pushed back to their original walls' in 1656 (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page). Highlands dropped as in nguyen-lords_1572.

correction.text: the 1659 outline (93,856 km2) for 1656-1658, without Hà Tĩnh and without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1656-1658 on the 1659 outline: Hà Tĩnh back with the Trịnh after the Nguyễn were 'pushed back to their original walls'; Khánh Hòa stays Nguyễn. Highlands dropped as in nguyen-lords_1572.

1659-1690: 93,856 km2, Quảng Bình to Khánh Hòa (14 of 16 cells). The Nguyễn hold Kauthara from 1653; the Panduranga page puts the Cham rump at Phan Rang, outside the shape. Applies to 1697 (not 1690) because the Saigon cells of the 1691 outline are dated to 1698 (Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page, see ledger 1698); highlands dropped as in nguyen-lords_1572.

correction.text: the 1659 outline, without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells; applies 1659-1697

keyframe_review.note: 1698-1699 (Cliopatria: 1691-1699): 94,596 km2; the southern edge drops from 11.8 to 10.7 N, a change of two Saigon cells. The Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page dates the first Nguyễn administration there to 1698 ('In 1698, Canh was sent by Nguyễn Phúc Chu to the south. He founded Gia Dinh garrison there'; 'founded the city of Saigon in 1698'), so the shape holds from 1698, not 1691; the Nguyễn lords page lists invasions of Cambodia 'in 1658, 1690, 1691, 1697 and 1713' without naming land. The 1692 occupation of Panduranga (Ninh Thuận and Bình Thuận, outside the shape) is in the ledger as an occupation. Highlands dropped as in nguyen-lords_1572.

correction.text: the 1691 outline (Cliopatria) with the Saigon cells, without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells; applies 1698-1699

the Nguyễn outline of 1700 plus the Mekong delta and the Đồng Nai, Bình Dương and Tây Ninh lowlands that Cliopatria draws as 'Cambodia' (163 cells of its 271), without its Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận cells (28, Panduranga) and its Lâm Đồng, Đắk Nông, Bình Phước and Đắk Lắk uplands (80), without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: 1700-1701: the Nguyễn outline plus the delta lowlands (163 cells of Cliopatria's 'Cambodia' 271), under 'full Vietnamese administrative control' (Post-Angkor page; the delta only). The first version took all 271 cells; 28 of them are Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận (Panduranga), a Cham client from 1695 (ledger 1695; champa draws it as Cham land 1695-1832) and 77 are the Lâm Đồng, Đắk Nông and Bình Phước uplands, which no page names, so both are out. Tây Ninh (13 cells) and the Đồng Nai lowlands are kept as Cliopatria's reading; no page dates them. The 17 western Gulf-of-Siam cells are not Nguyễn until 1755 (the Mạc Cửu page has Hà Tiên Cambodian until 1714).

correction.text: the Nguyễn outline of 1702 plus the delta lowlands ('Cambodia' row without Panduranga and the uplands); without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: 1702-1708: same treatment as nguyen-lords_1700; the Nguyễn outline changes little from 1700 (318 cells with the highlands in Cliopatria).

correction.text: the Nguyễn outline of 1709 plus the delta lowlands ('Cambodia' row without Panduranga and the uplands); applies 1709-1754; without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: 1709-1754: same treatment as nguyen-lords_1700. The 17 western cells (Hà Tiên and Rạch Giá coast) are Cambodian or Mạc until 1755: the Mạc Cửu page has 'Hà Tiên was a part of Cambodia until the year 1714' and a Nguyễn title for Mạc Cửu from 1708, and the Nguyễn lords page has the Nguyễn 'secured a port on the Gulf of Siam' only in 1755.

correction.text: the 1757 Nguyễn outline (Cliopatria 102,119 km2 with the highlands) plus the delta lowlands, with the Gulf of Siam port secured in the 1755 campaign; without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: 1755-1756: the 1757 outline already holds 15 of the 17 western cells, which is the 1755 gain (ledger). Highlands dropped as in nguyen-lords_1572; Panduranga and the uplands out as in nguyen-lords_1700.

correction.text: the 1757 Nguyễn outline plus the delta lowlands; applies 1757-1772; without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1757-1772. 102,119 km2; the page gives no area and no 1757 event ('Tầm Phong Long' is not on the pages opened), so the growth is read from the 1755 campaign. The delta is added as in 1700. Panduranga and the uplands are out as in nguyen-lords_1700; highlands dropped as in nguyen-lords_1572.

correction.text: the 1757 outline without Bình Định (Quy Nhơn, taken by the Tây Sơn in 1773) plus the delta lowlands; without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 1773-1774: 'In 1773 the Tây Sơn captured the port of Qui Nhơn' (Tây Sơn page), after the revolt of 1771 'against the Nguyễn lord'. Bình Định is Tây Sơn land from 1773 although Cliopatria keeps it Nguyễn to 1774. Panduranga, the uplands and the highlands are out as in the earlier keyframes.

correction.text: Gia Định and the delta lowlands, the last Nguyễn land (1775-1777), contested by the Tây Sơn from 1776; without Panduranga and the uplands

keyframe_review.note: Applies 1775-1777 (187 cells). Cliopatria's 8,428 km2 (24 cells, Gia Định only) leaves out the delta, which Cliopatria draws as 'Cambodia' (163 of its 271 cells are kept here). The Trịnh took Huế in February 1775 and 'Nguyễn retreated to Quảng Nam, and later to Gia Định'; the Nguyễn Nhạc page has 'the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận' occupied by the Tây Sơn after Lord Thuần fled to Gia Định, so Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa go with Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi (ledger 1775); the Tây Sơn took Gia Định in 1776 and the lords were destroyed in 1777. What Cliopatria's 1773 shape holds beyond this one is Thuận Hóa (ledger February 1775), Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi, Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa (ledger 1775) and the Central Highlands, which this dossier no longer draws.

region.text: Thuận Hóa, Quảng Nam and the coast to Phú Yên, without the Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk) and the Lâm Đồng and Đắk Nông edge cells

ledger.note: 1572: the Nguyễn lords stand as the south of the Lê court. The page's lords list begins with Nguyễn Hoàng in 1558 ('Subordinates of Trịnh lords (1558-1627)', 'de jure fief within the Lê dynasty'); the map separates the south from the Lê in 1572, the year Cliopatria and the Lê dossier hand over.
1600: the seat moves from Trà Bát to Dinh Cát (infobox 'Trà Bát (1570-1600)', 'Dinh Cát (1600-1626)'); Nguyễn Hoàng broke with the Trịnh-led court in 1600 (Trịnh lords page).

region.text: Kauthara, which the page places in Khánh Hòa province

ledger.note: 1611: the Nguyễn attack Panduranga. 'In 1611, in an attempt to retake land from the Nguyen lord, Champa mounted an attack in Phu Yen' and 'lord Nguyen Phuc Nguyen sent an army led by Văn Phong, a Cham defector, attacking Panduranga'; the page says it annexed 'the entire Kauthara Principality' yet also that Kauthara was lost only in 1653, so Khánh Hòa is drawn as contested until 1653.
1626: the seat moves to Phước Yên (infobox 'Dinh Cát (1600-1626)', 'Phước Yên (1626-1636)').
1636: the seat moves to Kim Long (infobox 'Kim Long (1636-1687)'); the page text puts the move to Phú Xuân in 1636, which the infobox does not.

region.text: Kauthara, which the page places in Khánh Hòa province

ledger.note: 1653: Kauthara falls. 'the Kauthara principality was lost to the Nguyen after a counterattack in 1653'; the page lists invasions of Panduranga in 1611, 1629, 1653 and 1692.

region.text: Kauthara, which the page places in Khánh Hòa province

ledger.note: 1653: the Nguyễn annex Kauthara. Khánh Hòa (the page places Kauthara in Khánh Hòa province) passes from Champa; Cliopatria's Nguyễn outline grows from 4 to 14 of its 16 cells.

region.text: Hà Tĩnh, taken after Quảng Bình

ledger.note: 1653: the Nguyễn invade the north. 'The Nguyễn invaded the north and captured Quảng Bình, then Hà Tĩnh'; in 1654 they attacked Nghệ An and were defeated by Trịnh Tạc's counterattack.

region.text: Hà Tĩnh, returned to the Trịnh

ledger.note: 1656: the Nguyễn 'were pushed back to their original walls' and give up Hà Tĩnh; Cliopatria keeps them there until 1658.

region.text: the Mekong delta, a hitherto Khmer domain

ledger.note: 1658: the Nguyễn first intervene in Cambodia. 'The first Vietnamese military intervention took place in 1658-59, in which rebel Cambodian princes...' (Post-Angkor page); the Nguyễn page lists invasions 'in 1658, 1690, 1691, 1697 and 1713'. By 1620 the Vietnamese 'had reached the Mekong Delta, a hitherto Khmer domain' and Chey Chettha allowed a customs post at Prey Nokor about 1623.
1687: the seat returns to Phú Xuân (infobox 'Phú Xuân (1687-1712, 1738-1775)').

region.text: Panduranga, the Cham principality around Phan Rang

ledger.note: 1692: Panduranga occupied. 'In 1692, lord Nguyễn Phúc Chu invaded Panduranga, arresting King Po Saut'; the Nguyễn renamed it Trấn Thuận Thành. Hatched, not annexed.

region.text: Panduranga, the Cham principality around Phan Rang

ledger.note: 1694: the Cham king is restored. 'In 1694, Panduranga king Po Saktiraydapatih (r. 1695-1727) received the title King of Thuan Thanh' after revolts of 1693-96.

region.text: Panduranga, the Cham principality around Phan Rang

ledger.note: 1695: Panduranga a Nguyễn client. 'From 1695 onward, Panduranga had been reduced to a client state of the Nguyen domain'; a treaty of 1712 restored the Cham monarchy as a Nguyễn vassal. The relation outlasts this dossier (annexed by Vietnam in 1832, infobox).

region.text: the Saigon cells added to the 1659 outline (Gia Định)

ledger.note: 1698: the Nguyễn found Gia Định and Saigon. 'In 1698, Canh was sent by Nguyễn Phúc Chu to the south. He founded Gia Dinh garrison there' and 'Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh founded the city of Saigon in 1698' (Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page; the Mekong expeditions 'placed the region firmly under Vietnamese administrative control', undated). Cliopatria's Nguyễn outline reaches the Saigon cells from 1691 (a two-cell change); the page's 1698 replaces that year. The Nguyễn lords page lists invasions of Cambodia in 1690, 1691 and 1697 without land.

region.text: the Mekong delta, a hitherto Khmer domain

ledger.note: 1699: the delta contest is closed in the ledger. Bridging: the Post-Angkor page gives no treaty or last battle, only that 'by the end of the 17th century, the region was under full Vietnamese administrative control'; the sibling post-angkor-cambodia ledger closes its contest in 1699. The Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page puts the Battle of Kampot and the capture of Phnom Penh in 1700, so the fighting moved into the Cambodian core after the delta was secured; that is outside the delta zone.

region.text: the Mekong delta and the Đồng Nai, Bình Dương and Tây Ninh lowlands that Cliopatria draws as 'Cambodia' (163 cells of its 271), without its Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận cells (28, Panduranga) and its Lâm Đồng, Đắk Nông, Bình Phước and Đắk Lắk uplands (80)

ledger.note: 1700: the Mekong delta passes under Nguyễn administration. 'By the end of the 17th century, the region was under full Vietnamese administrative control' and 'Cambodia gradually lost control of the Mekong Delta' (Post-Angkor page, which names only the Mekong Delta); the Nam tiến page: 'by diplomacy and by force', undated; Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh founded Gia Định and Saigon in 1698 and his expeditions 'placed the region firmly under Vietnamese administrative control', undated. The year is Cliopatria's (its Khmer Empire row loses the delta in 1700); the sibling dossier records the same loss. Fixed after review: the first version took all 271 cells of Cliopatria's 'Cambodia' row, which include Bình Thuận (27 cells) and Ninh Thuận (1), Panduranga, a Cham client from 1695 (ledger 1695), and 77 cells of Lâm Đồng, Đắk Nông and Bình Phước uplands plus 3 of Đắk Lắk; none is on the Post-Angkor page. The Gulf of Siam strip stays out until 1755.
1712: the seat moves to Bác Vọng (infobox 'Bác Vọng (1712-1738)').

region.text: Cambodia

ledger.note: 1715: the Siamese invade Cambodia against Nguyễn backing. 'A Vietnamese army under Trần Thượng Xuyên and Nguyễn Cửu Phú was sent to Cambodia to help Ang Em' (1714); in 1715 the Cambodian king 'asked for military assistance from the Annamites', 'Annam sent 25,000 troops' and 'the Siamese army was unable to capture Battambang province' (Ang Em page). Mirror of ayutthaya-kingdom's 1715 contest; the page's troop figures are internally inconsistent and the years, not the numbers, are used.

region.text: Cambodia

ledger.note: 1717 (end not dated by the page): 'In 1717, the Siamese king sent his army to invade Cambodia for the second time', 'Annam agreed by sending 50,000 troops'; 'The four Siamese armies that invaded Cambodia were all defeated', 'the remaining Siamese troops were withdrawn back to Ayutthaya' and 'The Siamese stopped the war and negotiated'. The Siamese-Vietnamese wars table instead calls 1717 a Siamese victory; no border change is recorded (see ayutthaya-kingdom).
1738: the seat returns to Phú Xuân (infobox 'Phú Xuân (1687-1712, 1738-1775)').

region.text: the delta's coastal land on the Gulf of Siam

ledger.note: 1739: Cambodian counterattack on the coast. 'After Cambodian raids' the Vietnamese 'secured their hold on the rich Mekong Delta'; 'Cambodians tried to reclaim lost coastal land; fighting lasted about ten years' (Nguyễn lords page, paraphrased in part). Region read as the Gulf coast of the delta.

region.text: the delta's coastal land on the Gulf of Siam

ledger.note: About 1749: the fighting ends. The page says only that it 'lasted about ten years' from 1739; no end year.

region.text: the 17 western cells of the 1700 'Cambodia' outline, the Gulf of Siam coast around Hà Tiên and Rạch Giá

ledger.note: 1755: a port on the Gulf of Siam. 'The Nguyễn mounted another campaign against Cambodia in 1755' and 'had secured a port on the Gulf of Siam'. The strip is the 17 western cells of Cliopatria's Cambodia outline, which its Nguyễn row takes in 1757; the pages do not name Hà Tiên or Tầm Phong Long. Mạc Cửu page: 'Hà Tiên was a part of Cambodia until the year 1714' (a footnote: he offered Hà Tiên province to the Nguyễn that year), a tribute mission and Nguyễn titles in 1708, a Cambodian invasion of Hà Tiên with Siamese support in 1715, and a Siamese expedition that overthrew its government in 1771; the strip is drawn Nguyễn only from 1755, the Nguyễn lords page's year, and Hà Tiên as a Mạc dependency has no dossier (see notes).

region.text: the port of Qui Nhơn and its province

ledger.note: 1773: the Tây Sơn take Qui Nhơn. 'In 1773 the Tây Sơn captured the port of Qui Nhơn' after the 1771 revolt 'against the Nguyễn lord'; Bình Định is my reading of the port's province.

region.text: the walls north of Huế and the land behind them

ledger.note: 15 November 1774: the Trịnh attack. 'Trịnh Sâm attacked, and for the first time the Nguyễn walls were broken' (Trịnh-Nguyễn War page), ending a border that 'was strongly guarded but peaceful' for 100 years.

region.text: Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi, Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa: 'the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận was occupied by Tây Sơn rebels'

ledger.note: 1775: the south-central coast from Quảng Nam to Khánh Hòa goes to the Tây Sơn. Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'Several months later, when the Tây Sơn army took Quảng Nam, Thuần had to flee to Gia Định' and 'Not long after, the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận was occupied by Tây Sơn rebels'; no year, but the sequence follows the Trịnh capture of Huế (Trịnh–Nguyễn War page: the Nguyễn 'retreated to Quảng Nam, and later to Gia Định'). Widened after review from Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi to Phú Yên (19 cells) and Khánh Hòa (14), which Cliopatria's 1773 shape holds and its 1775 shape does not; the Tây Sơn dynasty and Nguyễn Nhạc pages are silent on Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa as separate conquests (the latter says only that Nhạc later held Quy Nhơn, Quảng Ngãi and Phú Yên). Bình Thuận, in the same sentence, is Panduranga (a client, ledger 1695), not drawn as direct land. Bình Định went in 1773.
1775: the court flees to Quảng Nam and then Gia Định (infobox 'Quảng Nam (1775)', 'Gia Định (1775-1777, ...)').

region.text: Panduranga, the Cham principality around Phan Rang

ledger.note: 1775: the Nguyễn lose Panduranga with the coast. Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'Not long after [Lord Thuần fled to Gia Định], the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận was occupied by Tây Sơn rebels' (no year). The Panduranga page is silent on the 1770s and on Tây Sơn; it keeps the capital at Phan Rí Cửa until 1832, and the page's Nguyễn client relation (from 1695) is the Nguyễn successors' to carry on (the nguyen-dynasty dossier). Before review this event closed in 1777 only because the dossier ends.

region.text: Thuận Hóa, read as the three modern provinces

ledger.note: February 1775: the Trịnh take Huế. 'February 1775: The Trịnh captured Huế, the Nguyễn capital.'

region.text: Thuận Hóa, read as the three modern provinces

ledger.note: 1775: Thuận Hóa lost. Infobox 'Territorial changes: Trịnh captured Phú Xuân in 1775; Nguyễn retreated to Quảng Nam, and later to Gia Định'; the Hoàng Ngũ Phúc page makes the Trịnh general viceroy of Thuận Hóa. The provinces are my reading of Thuận Hóa.

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1776: the Tây Sơn take Gia Định. 'in 1776 the Tây Sơn army captured the last Nguyễn stronghold of Gia Định' (Tây Sơn page); the Nguyễn page has the lords destroyed 'by 1777' and the lords list shows Nguyễn Phúc Dương co-ruling in 1776-1777, so 1776 is drawn as a contest.

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1777: the contest ends with the lords' destruction. 'By 1777, Gia Định was captured and nearly the entire Nguyễn family was killed.' [fx-42: the lords do not end here; Ánh retakes the delta in 1778 (ledger/34) and the rump runs to 1785.]

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1777: Gia Định and the delta pass to the Tây Sơn. Trịnh-Nguyễn War page: the Nguyễn lords 'collapsed in Saigon in 1777'; Nguyễn Ánh alone 'managed to flee to Siam'.

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1778: Nguyễn Ánh retakes Gia Định. Quang Trung page: 'Nguyễn Ánh returned and occupied Gia Định in the next year' (the year after 1777, so 1778); Gia Long page: 'In late 1777, the main part of the Tây Sơn army left Saigon to go north', after which Ánh 'stealthily returned to the mainland' and reclaimed Saigon. The region is the delta of ledger/33, the land the Tây Sơn took in 1777. Mirrors tay-son-dynasty ledger/7, which names nguyen-dynasty (alive only from 1788) as counterpart. [Added fx-42, 2 Nov 2026, for the dossier requests R100 and R103: the Mekong delta was nobody's land 1778-1781.]

1780: 'In 1780, in an attempt to strengthen his political status, Nguyễn Phúc Ánh proclaimed himself Nguyễn vương' (Gia Long page). Nguyễn lords page infobox: lordship 'Dates 1558-1777, 1780-1802', capital 'Gia Định (1775-1777, 1780-1783, 1788-1802)'. [Added fx-42.]

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1782: the Tây Sơn retake Gia Định. 'In 1782, a Tây Sơn army under Nguyễn Nhạc and Nguyễn Huệ reoccupied Gia Định' and 'Nguyễn Ánh had to flee to Phú Quốc' (Quang Trung page). Gia Long page: 'In October 1782, the tide shifted again' and 'A counterattack by the Tây Sơn in early 1783 saw a heavy defeat to the Nguyễn'; the swing back is drawn as the 1783 contest. Mirrors tay-son-dynasty ledger/9. [Added fx-42.]

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1783: Gia Định changes hands again. Gia Long page: 'A counterattack by the Tây Sơn in early 1783 saw a heavy defeat to the Nguyễn' and Ánh 'again fled to Phu Quoc'; Quang Trung page: 'In 1783, Nguyễn Ánh and his supporters retreated to Siam with Siamese army.' Mirrors tay-son-dynasty ledger/10 (the delta is a contested zone 1783-1785; the Tây Sơn keep the ground). [Added fx-42.]

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 20 January 1785: the Siamese fleet called in by Ánh is destroyed ('the morning of 20 January 1785'), the Tây Sơn reach Gia Định in 1785, and 'Thepharirak and Nguyễn Ánh fled back to Bangkok' (Quang Trung page); Gia Long page: Ánh 'a refugee in Siam in 1785', there 'until August 1787'. Mirrors tay-son-dynasty ledger/12-13. [Added fx-42.]

region.text: Gia Định and the delta (without Panduranga and the uplands)

ledger.note: 1785: the rump state ends. Nguyễn lords page infobox: 'Rump state (1775-1785)' and 'Capital-in-exile: Bangkok (1785-1788)'; the delta is the Tây Sơn's until Nguyễn Ánh retakes Saigon on 7 September 1788 and founds the line of the nguyen-dynasty dossier (Gia Long page: 'captured Saigon on 7 September 1788'). The 1777 end of the first version moved here (fx-42, 2 Nov 2026) because the page runs the lordship 1558-1777 and 1780-1802 and the Tây Sơn ledger fights Ánh over Gia Định to 1785.

wars.name: Nguyễn–Cham wars

zones.text: Panduranga, occupied 1692-1694 and a client from 1695

wars.outcome: Nguyễn victory: Kauthara annexed in 1653; Panduranga occupied in 1692, restored in 1694 as King of Thuận Thành and a client state from 1695.
wars.note: 'repeatedly invaded Panduranga in 1611, 1629, 1653, 1692' (Panduranga page); the Nguyễn page has wars against Champa in 1611, 1629, 1653 and 1692 and says 'by 1693 the Cham leadership had succumbed to the Nguyen domination'.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (first phase)

zones.text: the Nguyễn walls north of Huế, held against offensives in 1633, 1642-43, 1648, 1661 and 1671

wars.outcome: Indecisive: the walls held; the Nguyễn invaded the north in 1653 and were pushed back by 1656; peace in 1673 with the Linh River as the border, for about a hundred years.
wars.note: Infobox 1627-1672 (intermittent); the text has peace in 1673. Open warfare from 1627 'with the next successor of the Trịnh, Trịnh Tráng' (Nguyễn lords page).

wars.name: Nguyễn campaigns in Cambodia
wars.outcome: Nguyễn gains: the Mekong delta under full Vietnamese administration by the end of the 17th century, a Gulf of Siam port secured in 1755.
wars.note: The page lists invasions in 1658, 1690, 1691, 1697 and 1713, support for Ang Em in 1714, the Cambodian effort of 1739 and a campaign in 1755. The Post-Angkor page dates the first intervention to 1658-59.

wars.name: Siamese–Nguyễn struggle for Cambodia (1714-1717)
wars.outcome: Inconclusive: a Vietnamese army helped Ang Em in 1714; the Siamese invasions of 1715 and 1717 failed to take Battambang and were withdrawn, and Siam 'stopped the war and negotiated'; no border change is recorded.
wars.note: Barom Ramadhipati (Ang Em) page: the Annamite troops of 1715 and 1717 are given as 25,000 plus 70,000 of Ang Em's own, and 50,000; the Nguyễn lords page has the Nguyễn sending an army to support Ang Em in 1714, who was allowed the crown in exchange for pledging allegiance to Siam. Mirrors ayutthaya-kingdom's 1715-1717 contest.

wars.name: Taksin's war against the Nguyễn (1769)
wars.outcome: No territorial result recorded on the page: 'War was launched against the Nguyễn in 1769' under King Taksin.

wars.name: Tây Sơn rebellion against the Nguyễn
wars.outcome: Tây Sơn victory: Qui Nhơn captured in 1773, Gia Định in 1776; the Nguyễn lords destroyed by 1777 except Nguyễn Ánh, who fled to Siam.

wars.name: Trịnh–Nguyễn War (second phase)
wars.outcome: Trịnh and Tây Sơn victory: the Trịnh captured Phú Xuân in February 1775; the Nguyễn retreated to Quảng Nam and later to Gia Định.

certainty.note: The Cham frontier and the Khmer delta are approximate; the Central Highlands are not drawn (no page puts them under the Nguyễn); the northern wall near Đồng Hới is a fixed line but unsurveyed.

The northern border with the Trịnh is fixed by the 1673 peace (Gianh or Linh River) and is the one sharp line; the Cham, Cambodian and delta frontiers stay soft (the Gulf of Siam strip and Tây Ninh especially), so the era is soft. 1778-1785: the rump of Nguyễn Ánh holds Gia Định and the delta at soft frontiers.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 9 shapes, all reviewed; new keyframes 1656, 1755 and 1773. The pages give no area, so the infobox check could not be made.
Main decision: Cliopatria's 'Cambodia' row (slug cambodia, 1700-1802) is the 295-cell land that its Khmer Empire row loses in 1700 (287 cells in the row) and shares no cell with the Nguyễn outline. Only part of it is drawn here: 163 cells (the delta and the Đồng Nai, Bình Dương and Tây Ninh lowlands) are Nguyễn land from 1700 (the 17 western Gulf of Siam cells from 1755), following the Post-Angkor page ('by the end of the 17th century ... under full Vietnamese administrative control', which names only the Mekong Delta) and the sibling post-angkor-cambodia dossier (loss to nguyen-lords in 1700). Bình Thuận and Ninh Thuận (28 cells, Panduranga) are left to champa as a Nguyễn client from 1695 and the Lâm Đồng, Đắk Nông, Bình Phước and Đắk Lắk uplands (80 cells) are not drawn. The cambodia dossier is a null row (found and dissolve only). The Central Highlands (Kon Tum, Gia Lai, Đắk Lắk, 133 of the 296 cells of Cliopatria's 1572 outline) are not drawn either: no page puts them under the Nguyễn.
Counterparts not mirrored: champa's ledger (written) carries 1611 loss of Phú Yên, which the Panduranga page contradicts (Champa 'attempt to retake land' there in 1611, so the Nguyễn held it before); 1653 Kauthara and 1692-1694 occupation match. post-angkor-cambodia (written) matches the 1700 loss but has no mirror for the 1739-1749 contest and the 1755 gain, which name it here (the cambodia dossier no longer carries them). ayutthaya-kingdom's 1715-1717 contest is now mirrored (fix pass). tay-son-dynasty, nguyen-dynasty and thonburi-kingdom are not yet written: they should carry the 1773, 1775 (Quảng Nam to Khánh Hòa) and 1776-1777 gains and the 1777 successor line. The Nguyễn client Panduranga should be carried on by nguyen-dynasty to 1832. Hà Tiên (Mạc clan) has no dossier.
Ends: Cliopatria's row ends 1775; the page ends the lords in 1777 (and 1780-1802 for Nguyễn Ánh). The Tây Sơn page has Gia Định captured in 1776, the Nguyễn page 'by 1777', the Trịnh lords page 'the Nguyễn lost Saigon' in 1776; 1776 is drawn as a contest and 1777 as the end.
Not on the pages: 1708 Hà Tiên as a transfer (the Mạc Cửu page has a 1708 tribute mission and titles and Hà Tiên Cambodian until 1714), 1732 Mỹ Tho and Vĩnh Long, 1757 Tầm Phong Long, Côn Đảo, Hoàng Sa; the 1620 marriage alliance with Chey Chettha II is on the Nguyễn page without territory; 1674-1679, 1688, 1699 Cambodian events. The Gianh River line (page) is nine cells south of Cliopatria's northern edge; left as drawn. Dated in the fix pass: 1698 Gia Định and Saigon (Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh page).
Fix pass after review (2026-10-19): highlands dropped from keyframes 1572-1775; 1700 gain and unions minus Panduranga and the uplands; 1775 loss widened to Phú Yên and Khánh Hòa (Nguyễn Nhạc page: 'the country from Quảng Ngãi to Bình Thuận was occupied by Tây Sơn rebels', undated; the Tây Sơn dynasty page is silent on both); Nguyễn Hoàng from 1572; 1691 gain re-dated to 1698; 1715-1717 contest with ayutthaya-kingdom mirrored; Panduranga's vassal end 1775. Eight pages opened in the fix pass: five new (Nguyễn Nhạc, Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh, Mạc Cửu, Cochinchina, Barom Ramadhipati) and three read again (Tây Sơn dynasty, Nguyễn lords, Panduranga); the Siamese–Vietnamese War (1717) URL was not found.
Page budget: 6 pages opened against 5 in the first run (Nam tiến was thin), then 5 new pages in the fix pass at the reviewer's request (11 listed in all).
Fix pass fx-42 (2 Nov 2026), dossier requests R100 and R103: the lords' life now runs to 1785 (infobox 'Rump state (1775-1785)') so that Nguyễn Ánh's Gia Định regime is a live opponent of the Tây Sơn: gain 1778, rename 1780 (Nguyễn vương), loss 1782, contest 1783-1785, dissolve 1785. The delta is landless between 1777 and 1778 and from 1782 (the Tây Sơn ledger holds it). R103's claim that nguyen-dynasty exists only from 1802 is wrong: that dossier starts on 7 September 1788 (Gia Long page: Saigon captured on 7 September 1788), so 1788-1801 was never a gap. Handoff: tay-son-dynasty ledger/7, 9, 10, 12 name nguyen-dynasty (not alive before 1788) as counterpart for the 1778-1785 events; nguyen-lords is now the live party.
